concept: A grid of cells in one hue from faint to full by value, with a 2px gap and a scale that says which end is more.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a heatmap in a rainbow scale from blue through green to red
default_to_avoid.why_not: a rainbow has no order a reader can see and fails colour blindness; Pane uses one hue from faint to full

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns no hue of its own, only white at opacities and one ink, and colour appears only where it states a status or marks a diagram
derivation.form: marks carry the data palette, which belongs to the content like a scene or a photo, and the frame around them owns no hue (D-031)

derivation.consequence: status is spoken in text as well as shown in colour
derivation.form: every value is also in direct labels, a tooltip and a table view, so nothing is read by colour alone

derivation.consequence: secondary text keeps the lowest opacity that still measured as passing; text halos count only where WCAG allows them
derivation.form: every word on the chart is in a text tone, never in a series colour

options: A one hue, faint to full
variants.picked: A one hue, faint to full
variants.reason: A is sequential, one hue light to dark (dataviz). B has no visible order. C is a table, which the table view already is.

cell.why: each cell is the first data hue at a strength set by its value

scale.why: the scale under the grid gives the lowest and highest values in the secondary tone

ramp.why: the ramp shows the hue from faint to full and turns in RTL

live.why: a hidden live line says the value in focus so a screen reader hears what the tooltip shows

@media forced-colors: active.why: in forced colours the cells keep their shade so the grid still reads

data-on.why: the cell in focus is outlined in the primary tone

opacity.why: a cell eases to its new strength when the data changes
